applies_to: CISI 2 (Shah and Parpola 1991) printed pp. 435-447, PDF 470-482
CISI 1 (Joshi and Parpola 1987) printed pp. 366-375, PDF 402-411 (same five columns, checked on printed p. 366)
unit: one record per catalogue entry (CISI number); pieces of a broken object printed on separate lines stay in the same record, their cells joined with ' // ' in printed order

printed_columns.key_text_summary: CISI number assigned to the object illustrated; piece numbers (1), (2) inserted between columns 1 and 2 when separate loose pieces of one broken object have different museum or excavation numbers

number of the object in the current version of the FC (Finnish concordance; Koskenniemi and Parpola 1979, 1980, 1982); FC numbers for Mohenjo-daro and Harappa are keyed to object numbers in the plates of the excavation reports; the key on p. 434 gives the FC ranges that belong to the old excavations of Mohenjo-daro and Harappa

excavation number or corresponding data; a surface-find mark; numbers in parentheses usually layers; ??? when data are not available or the object carries a wrong excavation number (discussion postponed to CISI 3); bold face marks an indistinct or uncertain number
printed_columns.example_form: letter code and number: DK nnnn, DK-C nnnn, DK-i nnn, HR nnnn, VS nnnn, SD nnnn, DM nnn, MN nn-nnn, UPM/MD-nnn, RWTH nnnn-nnnn; ??? when not available

printed_columns.key_text_summary: museum where the object is kept and its registration number(s); italic numbers beginning with a two-digit year (50 = 1950) refer to the accession catalogue of the National Museum of Pakistan, from which the object was transferred
printed_columns.example_form: code and number: MD nnn; MD nnn, 50.nnn; MD 50.nnn, MM nnn; MD, MM nnn; NMP 50.nnn; L, P-nnnn; HM nnnnn; EXB nnnn; (MD nnn, 50.nnn) now: KHP; a bare code (EXB, NMP) when no number is printed

printed_columns.key_text_summary: sources of the photographs (and the one drawing) published in the volume; the first reference covers all unspecified photographs; negative numbers follow the source name; side letters (A, a for impression, bis for a second photograph) precede the reference they qualify
printed_columns.example_form: source code and negative number, side letters before the reference: JL nnn; A: Si. n:nnnn; a: Si. nn:nnn; AV nnn; a: P nnnn; a bis: P nnn

transcription_conventions.uncertain_character: [a/b] two candidates; [?] one unreadable character; [??] an unreadable stretch; whole alternatives [candidate_a/candidate_b] where a reading and a competing reading differ in more than one character (used only in the recheck)
transcription_conventions.typeface: bold (uncertain number) and italic (NMP accession) are recorded only when visibly distinct; at the scan's resolution they mostly are not, so the parser identifies NMP accessions by the two-digit-year form instead
transcription_conventions.continuation: lines of one column within an entry joined by one space

parsed_fields.excavation: per piece: printed, status (printed, not-available, blank), area_code (leading letters, e.g. DK, DK-C, DK-i, HR, VS, SD, DM, MN, UPM/MD, RWTH, L), surface_find, layer
parsed_fields.museum_holdings: per piece: list of {code, number, nmp_accession, former, current, query_mark}; '(..) now: X' marks the bracketed holding as former and X as current
parsed_fields.holding_institutions: names of the current holding institutions from the codes
parsed_fields.museum_number_usable: a code with a number, or an NMP accession
parsed_fields.photo_sources: photograph source codes present in column 5
